   - Still unexplained after those rules for specific request ids: route per the routing table (load billing-handoff) with the ids and what you checked.

The line contains three requests, all recorded as HTTP 200, totaling **41,565,393 billed tokens**. Some customers reconcile Redwood token usage against internal estimates and may observe higher usage totals. The most common causes are (1) client retries and (2) streaming cancellation behavior.

This page provides a support-ready explanation and recommended mitigations.

[content > Key definitions]
- **Attempt**: a single request admitted by the Redwood API gateway (server-side).
- **Logical request**: what the customer thinks of as one user action; may map to multiple attempts if the client retries.

[content > Retries]
- Redwood usage is recorded per-attempt.
- If a client retries after a timeout or non-200 response, each admitted attempt can be billable.
- The Usage dashboard lists rows by **request_id** (attempt identifier)."}, {"chunk_id": "bd7b22c1c0705a35", "source": "confluence/customer-success-and-support/known-issues-and-workarounds/usage-accounting-retries-and-stream-cancellation", "title": "Usage accounting: retries and streaming cancellation", "status": "published", "updated": "2025-02-18", "section": "content > Support playbook (quick response blurb) | content > References", "text": "[content > Support playbook (quick response blurb)]

- **Always respect Retry-After** when provided.
- **Use exponential backoff with jitter**; do not retry immediately.
- **Cap retries** to avoid amplifying overload.

If `Retry-After` is present:

Yes. Redwood records usage **per server-admitted attempt**, so if a client retries after a timeout, each attempt that was admitted can appear separately in Usage and be billable. For a timed-out or cancelled stream, the admitted attempt may still bill prompt tokens and any completion tokens generated before cancellation.

I can’t tell from the invoice line alone which of the three requests were retries; the usage records don’t link them into retry chains.
